userStories.title: Manual compaction keeps the last turn
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make native manual compaction summarize older turns even when the model has a large context window.

**Motivation** — `/compact` printed `nothing to compact` after five turns on `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash[high]`.

**Approach** — A turn starts at a `user` message whose content does not start with `COMPACTION_SUMMARY_PREFIX`. `manualKeepTokens(messages, keepTurns)` finds the start of the `keepTurns`-th last turn and returns the sum of `estimateTokens` over that message and every message after it. With fewer turn starts than `keepTurns` it returns the sum over the whole array. `compactHistory` passes `Math.min(keepBudget(window, compaction), manualKeepTokens(messages, MANUAL_KEEP_TURNS))` to `prepareCompaction`, so a last turn larger than the automatic budget is still cut at a valid point inside it, as the automatic path would. Everything else about the manual path stays: no pin, `before_compaction` not dispatched, `compaction.enabled` ignored, nothing written before the summary returns. Automatic compaction and `keepBudget` are unchanged.

Baseline: plans with `keepBudget(resolution.contextWindow, resolution.compaction)`. Target: plans with `Math.min(keepBudget(...), manualKeepTokens(messages, MANUAL_KEEP_TURNS))`. New exports `MANUAL_KEEP_TURNS = 1` and `manualKeepTokens(messages: readonly TranscriptMessage[], keepTurns: number): number`. Summarizer rejection propagates, history unchanged. Mirror the seeded-transcript harness in packages/nax-agent/test/integration/session/native-manual-compaction.test.ts and add unit coverage for turn boundaries, summary markers and tool results.

**Scope** — In: manual-compaction.ts helpers and compactHistory planning with their unit/native-session integration regressions. Out: unread-call recovery (US-002), streaming events (US-003), TUI footer and title changes (US-005–US-007). The manual compaction keep (`MANUAL_KEEP_TURNS`) is a constant, not a config field; `keepRecentPercent` and automatic compaction are unchanged. `/compact` takes no focus-instructions argument.

**Interface**
```typescript
export const MANUAL_KEEP_TURNS = 1;
export function manualKeepTokens(messages: readonly TranscriptMessage[], keepTurns: number): number;
```

[unit] manualKeepTokens([u1, a1, u2, a2], 2) equals the sum of estimateTokens over all four messages.
[unit] manualKeepTokens([u1, a1], 2) equals the sum of estimateTokens over both messages.

[unit] manualKeepTokens does not count a user message whose content starts with COMPACTION_SUMMARY_PREFIX as a turn start: for [summary, a0, u1, a1] and keepTurns 1 it equals estimateTokens(u1) + estimateTokens(a1).

[integration] When the summarizer rejects during session.compact(), the rejection propagates and stored history remains unchanged, as today.

userStories.title: Recover once from unread native tool-call text
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Ask a native brain once to retry an unread literal tool-call block through the declared tool interface.

**Motivation** — A local model wrote `ScrashpadWrite` (a misspelt `ScratchpadWrite`) inside a `<tool_call>` block.

**Approach** — A built-in `before_turn_end` handler. It returns `{ followUp }` when all of these hold: `ended` is `"completed"`, `stopped` is `false`, `unreadToolCall.sent` is `false`, and the last message in `messages` is an `assistant` message whose text contains the literal `<tool_call>`. Otherwise it returns `{}`. Before returning a follow-up it sets `unreadToolCall.sent = true`, so a turn gets at most one. The follow-up text is:

```
Your reply contains a <tool_call> block that was not run: it did not read as a call of a declared tool. Call tools through the tool interface, using one of these exact names: <names>.
```

where `<names>` is `toolNames()` joined with `, `, or `(none)` when it is empty. A follow-up the loop then drops at `MAX_FOLLOW_UPS_PER_TURN` still counts as sent. The handler reads `toolNames` and `unreadToolCall` through `state.current` at dispatch, like the other built-ins, because `registerBuiltinLoopHandlers` repoints a reused registry rather than installing a second handler. The turn loop creates `{ sent: false }` once per turn, next to the spin flags, and passes `toolNames: () => tools.map((tool) => tool.name)`, reading the same `tools` array the round trips send. The handler is registered before the plugin entries, so a plugin's own `followUp` (a later handler's patch overwrites an earlier one) wins. The follow-up counts against `MAX_FOLLOW_UPS_PER_TURN` like any other.

`BuiltinLoopHandlerDeps` gains `readonly toolNames: () => readonly string[]` and `readonly unreadToolCall: { sent: boolean }`; `registerBuiltinLoopHandlers` registers a built-in `before_turn_end` handler before the plugin entries. Update packages/nax-agent/test/unit/native/session/loop-handlers-plugins.test.ts: its `install` helper builds a literal `BuiltinLoopHandlerDeps`; it gains `toolNames: () => []` and `unreadToolCall: { sent: false }`, and assertions on the handlers registered for `before_turn_end` now also see one built-in entry ahead of the plugin entries. Test scripted sessions and registry reuse, not a server-specific response extension.

**Scope** — In: native built-in handler, its per-turn dependencies, turn-loop wiring, and integration regressions. Out: compaction (US-001), streaming events (US-003) and ACP translation (US-004). The unread tool-call follow-up applies to native brains only; ACP brains are not changed. Recovery from an undeclared tool name relies on the `<tool_call>` text in the reply; nax does not read Strata's `strata_rejected_tool_calls` response field or any other server-specific field. No fuzzy matching or rewriting of a misspelt tool name; the model is asked to call again. A reply that quotes the literal `<tool_call>` text on purpose also gets the one follow-up; nax does not try to tell a quoted block from an unread call.

**Interface**
```typescript
readonly toolNames: () => readonly string[];
readonly unreadToolCall: { sent: boolean };
BeforeTurnEndPayload { messages, roundTrips, ended, stopped, followUpsSoFar }
BeforeTurnEndPatch { followUp? }
```
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] With a scripted model whose first reply is the text <tool_call>{"name":"ScrashpadWrite"}</tool_call> and whose second reply is done, the turn sends a second request whose last message is a user message starting Your reply contains a <tool_call> block that was not run.
[integration] That follow-up message lists every tool name the turn's first request declared, joined with `, `.
[integration] With a scripted model that replies with a <tool_call> text block on every round, the turn sends exactly two requests and ends completed.
[integration] With a scripted model whose only reply is plain text without <tool_call>, the turn sends exactly one request.
[integration] A turn whose round 1 reply is a real tool call and whose round 2 reply is <tool_call> text sends exactly one follow-up request after round 2.
[integration] When a plugin before_turn_end handler returns { followUp: "plugin text" } on a reply containing <tool_call>, the continuation request's last user message is plugin text.
[integration] A turn stopped by the invalid-call budget whose last assistant text contains <tool_call> sends no follow-up request.
[integration] A turn cancelled while its reply contains <tool_call> sends no follow-up request.
[integration] Two consecutive send() calls on one session, each whose first reply contains <tool_call>, each send one follow-up: the once-per-turn flag does not carry over.
[unit] The built-in before_turn_end handler returns {} and leaves unreadToolCall.sent false when the payload's last message is a user message.
[unit] With toolNames returning [], the handler's follow-up ends using one of these exact names: (none).

[integration] Two send() calls on one session that reuse one caller-supplied loop-event registry each send one follow-up for a reply containing <tool_call>: the repointed registry reads the second turn's fresh unreadToolCall.
[integration] A turn stopped by spin or deadline whose last assistant text contains <tool_call> sends no unread-tool-call follow-up request.

userStories.title: Emit and coalesce native tool-input deltas
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry argument-stream growth as count-only native session deltas.

**Motivation** — While the model streams a large `Write` call's arguments the working line stays on `Thinking…`: nax-ai yields `tool-call-partial` events, and `deltaOf` in `packages/nax-agent/src/native/stream-complete.ts` drops them.

**Approach** — `deltaOf` maps a `tool-call-partial` event to `{ type: "tool_input_delta", callId: id, name, chars }`, where `chars` is the growth of `rawInput.length` since the previous partial with the same `id` in this stream (the first partial's whole length). A partial whose length did not grow yields no delta. The emitter stamps the round as it does for text deltas, so the event reaches the `send()` iterator as a `SessionEvent` that the channel merges as described above. It carries only the name and a character count, never the argument text. The ACP server emits nothing for it. Adding the union member makes `translate` in `packages/nax-agent-acp` (an exhaustive switch with no default) fail to typecheck until US-004 adds its case: US-003's gates are scoped to `packages/nax-agent`, and US-004 is the next story, depending only on US-003.

In the chat TUI, `reduceTurnStatus` puts the turn in the `writing` phase and adds `chars` to `streamedChars`, so the working line reads `Writing…` and its `↓ ~N tokens` estimate grows. `reduceTranscript` leaves the transcript unchanged. `decodeRate` treats the event as a round's first output delta. Subagent events (`isSubagentEvent`) are ignored by all three, as today. This TUI integration is US-005, not this story.

`StreamDelta` target: `{ type: "text_delta" | "thinking_delta"; text: string }`, or `{ type: "tool_input_delta"; callId: string; name: string; chars: number }`. `TurnEvent` and `SessionEventBody`: both unions gain `{ readonly type: "tool_input_delta"; readonly round: number; readonly callId: string; readonly name: string; readonly chars: number }`. `DeltaEvent` includes `tool_input_delta`; two `tool_input_delta` events merge when `round` and `callId` match, into one carrying the summed `chars`.

Update packages/nax-agent/test/unit/native/stream-complete.test.ts — the shared `script` holds a `tool-call-partial` (`id: "c1"`, `name: "Read"`, `rawInput: "{"`), so "taps only text and thinking deltas, in stream order" now also receives `{ type: "tool_input_delta", callId: "c1", name: "Read", chars: 1 }` at that position; the expected list gains it and the test is renamed to say it taps text, thinking and tool-input deltas. In session-event-channel.test.ts a test that asserts only `text_delta` and `thinking_delta` merge holds for those two; `tool_input_delta` events with the same `round` and `callId` now merge, summing `chars`. Preserve collectStream folding, sink-error isolation, stream-local tracking and O(1) channel queuing.

**Scope** — In: stream-complete mapping, emitter delta type, both session event unions, channel classification/merge and native send regressions. Out: ACP translator case (US-004), TUI reduction/rate work (US-005). `tool_input_delta` events carry no argument text and are not recorded in transcripts, ledgers or ACP history.

**Interface**
```typescript
{ type: "text_delta" | "thinking_delta"; text: string }
{ type: "tool_input_delta"; callId: string; name: string; chars: number }
{ readonly type: "tool_input_delta"; readonly round: number; readonly callId: string; readonly name: string; readonly chars: number }
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] streamComplete with a delta sink, over a stream yielding tool-call-partial events for id c1 with rawInput lengths 5 then 12, calls the sink with { type: "tool_input_delta", callId: "c1", name, chars: 5 } then chars: 7.
[unit] A tool-call-partial whose rawInput length equals the previous partial's for the same id produces no sink call.
[unit] Partials for two ids c1 and c2 interleaved are measured per id: c2's first partial of length 4 yields chars: 4 after c1 reached 12.
[unit] A tool_input_delta sink call carries no text or rawInput field.

[integration] A native session send() whose scripted model streams one tool call's arguments in three partials yields tool_input_delta session events with that call's callId, name and the round of the request, before the tool_call event.
[integration] The chars of all tool_input_delta events for one call, summed, equal the length of that call's last tool-call-partial rawInput.

userStories.title: Show context tokens against effort-normalized model windows
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Restore context-window lookup for effort-qualified models and show tokens in use against that window.

**Motivation** — The footer's `N% ctx` span never appeared.

**Approach** — The cache fix: `catalogModel("opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash[high]")` yields `{ provider: "opencode-go", name: "deepseek-v4.1-flash" }`.

The footer span, with `tokens = status.contextTokens` and `window = state.contextWindow`:

| tokens | window | text | colour |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| undefined | any | no span | — |
| known | undefined or `<= 0` | `${formatTokens(tokens)} ctx` | muted |
| known | `> 0` | `${formatTokens(tokens)}/${formatWindow(window)} ctx (${percent}%)` | by `percent`, as today |

`percent` is `Math.round(tokens / window * 100)`, as today. `formatWindow(n)`: from 999,500 up, `n / 1000000` rounded to at most two decimals with trailing zeros dropped, then `M` (`999500` → `1M`, `1000000` → `1M`, `1050000` → `1.05M`); from 1,000 up, `Math.round(n / 1000)` then `k` (`200000` → `200k`, `262144` → `262k`); below 1,000, the number itself.

`catalogModel`: splits `parseModelSpec(model).model`, so the effort suffix never reaches the lookup; the cache stays keyed by the full model string. A catalog exception leaves the window unknown, so the span shows `<tokens> ctx`.

`contextSpan`, `contextPercent`, `percentColor`, and `formatTokens` with its constants (`TOKEN_UNIT`, `TOKEN_DECIMALS`, `TOKEN_SUFFIX`), move to a new module `packages/nax/src/tui/chat/context-span.ts` (`chat-status.ts` is at 591 of its 600-line cap), which also exports `formatWindow(n: number): string` and defines its own ` · ` separator constant. `context-span.ts` takes only type imports from `chat-status.ts` (`TurnStatus`, `ChatHostState`), so no value-import cycle forms (`packages/nax/scripts/baselines/import-cycles-baseline.json` is at 0). `chat-status.ts` value-imports `contextSpan` and `formatTokens` from it and re-exports `formatTokens` and `formatWindow`, so existing importers are unchanged. The span renders `<tokens>/<window> ctx (<percent>%)`, or `<tokens> ctx` with no window.

Update chat-status.test.ts CONTEXT_CASES to tokens/window with unchanged colors; unknown and zero windows now show `m1 · 36.0k ctx · $0.42`, unknown token count still has no span. Preserve existing provider/model split expectations in context-window-cache.test.ts and add effort stripping. Update chat-app-layout.test.tsx's footer and chat-compact.test.tsx's AFTER_PERCENT using each fixture's actual tokens/window, keeping the frame assertion otherwise unchanged.

**Scope** — In: cache lookup normalization, new context-span.ts, helper re-exports, footer text and regressions. Out: Writing phase changes (US-005), title animation (US-007), model override and Agent-card work (US-008/US-009). The context span is not shown before the first turn of a session, including a resumed one.

userStories.title: Animate the terminal title while chat is busy
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Animate the title's busy marker with one cancellable timer while preserving title restoration.

**Motivation** — The title's busy marker is static (`✳ nax · repo` for the whole turn), so a background tab gives no sign the chat is still working (#2797).

**Approach** — `titleFrames(glyphs)` returns `glyphs.spinner` when it has at least two frames, and otherwise `[glyphs.busy]`. `chatTitleFrame(project, frame)` returns `${frame} ` followed by the idle title (`nax · <project>` with control characters removed), i.e. `✶ nax · repo`. In `renderChat`:

- `busy(true)` writes `chatTitle(project, true, glyphs)` at once, as today, then arms one `_renderChatDeps.setTimeout` of `TITLE_FRAME_MS`. Each tick writes `setTitleSequence(chatTitleFrame(project, frames[i % frames.length]))` for `i = 0, 1, 2, …` and re-arms the next timeout. A second `busy(true)` while a timeout is armed arms no second one.
- `busy(false)` clears the armed timeout with `_renderChatDeps.clearTimeout` and writes the idle title.
- `restore` clears the armed timeout before it writes `POP_TITLE`; a tick never writes or re-arms after `restore`, and a `busy(true)` after `restore` arms nothing.

userStories.title: Read nested-project workflow state through repo
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Introduce a safe nested-project resolver and let the workflow state tool read the selected project's own artifacts.

**Motivation** — `nax chat` opened in a workspace folder (`projects/nax`) whose nax repo is nested (`repos/nax`) cannot plan, run or review there: every workflow and jobs tool is bound to the chat's own `repoRoot`, and restarting the chat in the nested repo loses the conversation.

**Approach** — `resolveTargetRepo(chatRoot: string, repo: unknown): Promise<{ readonly root: string } | { readonly error: string }>`, in `packages/nax/src/chat/target-repo.ts`, applies these rules in order:

1. `repo` undefined → `{ root: chatRoot }`.
2. `repo` not a string, or blank → `[chat] repo must be a non-empty string`.
3. `path.resolve(chatRoot, repo)` does not exist → `[chat] repo <repo> does not exist`.
4. Its real path is neither the real path of `chatRoot` nor inside it → `[chat] repo <repo> is outside <chatRoot>`. "Inside" is `isWithinRoot(path, root)`, exported from the same module: both arguments are real paths, and `path` equals `root` or starts with `root` followed by the path separator, so `/w/chat-evil` is not inside `/w/chat`.
5. Its real path equals the real path of `chatRoot` → `{ root: chatRoot }`.
6. It has no `.nax` directory → `[chat] repo <repo> is not a nax project: no .nax directory`.
7. Otherwise `{ root: <its real path> }`.

Where `repo` is accepted, a returned error becomes the tool's error result and nothing else happens (no approval card, no launch, no read).

`targetOutputDir(root: string): Promise<string>`, in the same module, returns the project output directory of the nax project at `root`, computed the way `composeChat` computes the chat's own: `projectOutputDir(getProjectKey(config, root), config.outputDir)` with `config = await loadConfig(join(root, ".nax"))`, loaded through an injectable `_targetRepoDeps.loadConfig`.

`When the nax project is in a folder inside this chat's folder (for example repos/nax), pass repo with that folder's path; the chat stays where it is.` This story adds the workflow line; US-011 adds the jobs line. Update workflow-provider.test.ts's exact inputSchema assertion to include `repo: { type: "string" }`. Use temporary real directories and symlinks for containment regressions, and an injected config loader for output-directory resolution.

**Motivation** — `nax chat` opened in a workspace folder (`projects/nax`) whose nax repo is nested (`repos/nax`) cannot plan, run or review there: every workflow and jobs tool is bound to the chat's own `repoRoot`, and restarting the chat in the nested repo loses the conversation.

Where `repo` is accepted, a returned error becomes the tool's error result and nothing else happens (no approval card, no launch, no read). Reuse resolveTargetRepo from US-010, respecting its ordered validation/canonical containment rules, and the resolved-root launch behavior supplied by US-011. Preserve repo across parseStep/parseChainStepInput/parseJobInput boundaries instead of accepting then discarding it; the current JobLaunchInput parser does not retain this optional value. Preserve plan spec resolution and step-numbered errors via stepError, plus existing bot PR placeholders, checks, cost caps and admission semantics. A step without repo still resolves its spec and argv against options.repoRoot. For a rejected step, do not read that step's target artifacts; resolveSteps is sequential, so earlier valid steps may already have resolved their own specs.

A chain's approval card keeps the chat's own `workdir` line; each step's nested root shows in its argv's `-d`. Update packages/nax/test/unit/chat/jobs/chain-argv.test.ts — "defines exactly the launch schema fields" pins `CHAIN_STEP_FIELDS` with an exact equality; every kind's list gains `repo`. Test proposal argv and subsequent auto-admitted launches together so canonical roots and repo-relative plan specs cannot diverge across the approval boundary.

**Scope** — In: CHAIN_STEP_FIELDS, step input propagation, per-step repo/spec/argv resolution and chain/launch parity regressions. Out: resolver implementation/workflow state (US-010), launch schemas/runner/write guard (US-011). A chain's approval card keeps the chat's own `workdir` line; each step's nested root shows in its argv's `-d`. `repo` reaches only nax projects inside the chat's folder; a sibling or parent folder is refused.

**Interface**
```typescript
resolveTargetRepo(chatRoot: string, repo: unknown): Promise<{ readonly root: string } | { readonly error: string }>
CHAIN_STEP_FIELDS
```
